name: Chair A, Chair B
why_it_works: People pick service providers by how the appointment feels, not by credentials. Putting the viewer in the chair from first-person view lets them feel the rushed appointment and the attentive one in their own body, so trust is felt before any claim is made.

hook.pattern: First-person POV: you sit down twice, in two chairs, and feel the difference in the first ten seconds.
examples: POV: same appointment, two different chairs.
Chair A rushes you. Chair B asks one question first.
You can tell in ten seconds which chair to trust.

variables.name: rushed_moment
variables.description: What a rushed appointment feels like
variables.example: clippers on before you finish your sentence

variables.name: first_question
variables.description: The question you always ask first (spoken; 12 words or fewer)
variables.example: How do you want it to look in two weeks, not today?

variables.name: detail_list
variables.description: Three small things you always do
variables.example: consult, hot towel, mirror check from the back

visual.prompt: First-person POV vertical 9:16 photo looking at two empty service chairs side by side, left under harsh flat light labeled A, right under warm soft light labeled B, inviting {{brand}} interior
First-person POV vertical shot from a service chair, a provider's hands moving quickly into frame, glancing at a phone, harsh overhead light, slightly hurried camera shake, faces cropped out
First-person POV vertical shot from a service chair at {{brand}}, a provider leans in at eye level and listens, warm soft light, calm steady camera, genuine attentive expression
Vertical close-up detail photo of a careful finishing step during {{appointment}} at {{brand}}, warm light, tidy tools in soft focus, premium feel

beats.voiceover: You felt the difference before anything happened.

visual.prompt: First-person POV vertical photo looking into a mirror at {{brand}}, the provider smiling behind, relaxed atmosphere, warm light, face of the client out of frame

craft.notes: Keep the camera at seated eye height the whole time so the viewer is the customer. Chair A should be normal-busy, not villainous: one rushed moment is enough. The first question in Chair B is the line people will quote back to you.

do_not: Make Chair A look like a specific real local business
Show a patient's or client's face, chart or account details without written consent
Turn Chair B into a list of credentials; this ad is about feeling, not résumé
compliance: Med spa: no before/after results in this ad unless paired with 'results vary' and a documented patient consent; no promises of outcome
Dental and chiropractic: no claims of cures or guaranteed relief; follow your state board's advertising rules
Financial advisors: no promises of returns or income; include required firm disclosures and do not imply the attentive meeting guarantees performance
